name: MicroPython for Raspberry Pi Pico

instructions: Unplug the Pico if it is currently powered.
Hold down the BOOTSEL button on the Pico.
While holding BOOTSEL, plug the Pico into your computer over USB.
Release BOOTSEL. A new drive named RPI-RP2 appears on your computer.
Drag firmware.uf2 onto the RPI-RP2 drive.
The drive ejects automatically once the copy finishes. MicroPython is now installed and the Pico reboots.

verify: After the drive disappears, the on-board LED blinks once. To start coding, install Thonny (https://thonny.org) and connect to the Pico over USB.
description: Official MicroPython firmware for the Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040). Drag-drop install via the Pico's USB-mass-storage bootloader. No browser flashing required — the Pico literally mounts as a USB drive. Once installed you can write and run Python directly on the chip using Thonny, the official IDE.
